newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong Motor denies merger rumour.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong Motor denies merger rumour.

text.p: Ssangyong Motor Co denied on Friday market rumours that the carmaking unit of South Korea's Ssangyong Group was a merger and acquisition target, a company spokesman said.
"It's totally groundless," Ssangyong Motor spokesman Joe Min-jyun told Reuters.
Brokers said shares in Ssangyong Motor were in the spotlight because of the market speculation. It rose 470 won to hit its upper limit and year high of 8,330 won in early Friday trade.
"The rumour might not be true. Some speculators, who had bought the shares at bargain prices, seem to be intentionally spreading the story," said a Coryo Securities broker.
Brokers said the rise was also in line with a recent rally in low-priced, large-capitalisation shares, which are expected to benefit from an anticipated interest rate cut.
Joe attributed the recent sharp rises to the stock's cheap price. "Our stock price looks undervalued," he said, suggesting 15,000 won would be a more reasonable level for the shares.

The brisk sales of four-wheel drives at home and abroad was another factor behind the climbs, he said. He forecast the company's turnover would reach 1.5 trillion this year from 890 billion a year earlier. -- Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5647
